activities.title: First Gemini Call and Response Anatomy
activities.document_title: Session 1 Class Activity 1 First Gemini Call and Response Anatomy
activities.overview: Create the shared Gemini helper, make one LangChain call, and inspect the returned AI message.
activities.primary_output: A working first_call.py program
instructions: Step 1  Create a folder named session_01 and open a terminal inside it.
Step 2  Install the packages listed above and confirm the same Python interpreter is selected in VS Code.
Step 3  Create .env with GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_key_here and GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash. Use a free-tier model that is available in your Google AI Studio project if this model is unavailable.
Step 4  Create .gitignore and add .env so the secret cannot be committed accidentally.
Step 5  Complete common.py. Load environment variables and return one ChatGoogleGenerativeAI object from create_model.
Step 6  Run first_call.py and inspect both the generated answer and the message metadata.
Step 7  Change only the topic in the prompt, run again, and write one sentence describing what changed.

activities.title: System Role Experiment
activities.document_title: Session 1 Class Activity 2 System Role Experiment
activities.overview: Keep the human question fixed and measure how three system instructions change the response.
activities.primary_output: Three controlled prompt trials and a comparison table
instructions: Step 1  Use the fixed question Why do programmers use APIs for all three trials.
Step 2  Create three roles: patient beginner teacher, technical interviewer, and visual analogy coach.
Step 3  Give every role an explicit format or length constraint so compliance can be evaluated.
Step 4  Run all trials with one model object and temperature 0.
Step 5  Save each output under a clear trial label.
Step 6  Complete a four-column observation table covering vocabulary, tone, format, and technical depth.
Step 7  Identify one instruction that the model followed well and one that it followed imperfectly.

activities.title: Beginner Concept Explainer
activities.document_title: Session 1 Home Task 1 Beginner Concept Explainer
activities.overview: Build a command-line tutor that adapts one explanation to the learner, topic, and requested format.
activities.primary_output: A reusable concept_explainer.py command-line program
instructions: Step 1  Ask the user for topic, learner level, and one format from paragraph, bullets, or steps.
Step 2  Strip whitespace and stop with a friendly error when any required value is empty.
Step 3  Construct a clear request containing the audience, required sections, word limit, and chosen format.
Step 4  Invoke one reusable Gemini model and print only the final learner-facing answer.
Step 5  Run the program for vector databases at high-school level in bullet format.
Step 6  Run a second case with an empty topic and confirm that the model is not called.
Step 7  Record the two test cases and observed results in test_notes.txt.

activities.title: Three Turn Study Buddy
activities.document_title: Session 1 Home Task 2 Three Turn Study Buddy
activities.overview: Maintain a short conversation by appending human and AI messages to one explicit history list.
activities.primary_output: A three-turn conversational study_buddy.py program
instructions: Step 1  Start the list with one SystemMessage defining a patient tutor, short answers, and one example per answer.
Step 2  Repeat three times: read a question, append HumanMessage, invoke the model with the full list, print the response, and append the returned AIMessage.
Step 3  For turn 1, ask What is an API. For turn 2, ask Give another example without repeating the topic. For turn 3, ask Quiz me on what we discussed.
Step 4  Print the role and a shortened preview of every message after the conversation ends.
Step 5  Run a comparison version that sends only the third question with no previous messages.
Step 6  Write a short explanation of why the two third-turn responses differ.

activities.title: Dynamic Prompt Template Lab
activities.document_title: Session 2 Class Activity 1 Dynamic Prompt Template Lab
activities.overview: Replace repeated prompt strings with one reusable chat template and inspect the formatted messages before calling Gemini.
activities.primary_output: A reusable dynamic_prompt_lab.py program
instructions: Step 1  Identify the parts that remain fixed: teacher role, analogy requirement, and maximum length.
Step 2  Choose three variables: topic, student_level, and output_format.
Step 3  Build a ChatPromptTemplate from one system message and one human message.
Step 4  Create three input dictionaries using different topics, levels, and formats.
Step 5  Invoke the template first and print the formatted messages for trial 1.
Step 6  Pass the formatted prompt to the model and print the response.
Step 7  Run all three trials and record which variable caused the clearest visible change.

activities.title: Structured Lesson Card
activities.document_title: Session 2 Class Activity 2 Structured Lesson Card
activities.overview: Use a Pydantic schema so Gemini returns a predictable lesson object instead of free-form text.
activities.primary_output: A validated LessonCard object and JSON file
instructions: Step 1  Define LessonCard with title, summary, analogy, key_points, check_question, and difficulty fields.
Step 2  Restrict difficulty to beginner, intermediate, or advanced using Literal.
Step 3  Add descriptions and sensible length constraints where appropriate.
Step 4  Wrap the Gemini model with with_structured_output using the LessonCard schema and json_schema method.
Step 5  Combine the chat prompt and structured model into a chain.
Step 6  Invoke the chain for embeddings and print each field separately.
Step 7  Save result.model_dump_json(indent=2) as lesson_card.json.
Step 8  Create one invalid LessonCard manually to observe Pydantic validation before submission.

activities.title: Personalized Interview Coach
activities.document_title: Session 2 Home Task 1 Personalized Interview Coach
activities.overview: Design one reusable chat prompt that creates role-specific interview practice and returns clean text through an output parser.
activities.primary_output: An interview_coach.py application with three test profiles
instructions: Step 1  Collect target_role, experience_level, difficulty, and focus_area in a dictionary.
Step 2  Write a system message defining the interviewer, fairness expectations, and concise style.
Step 3  Write a human template that requires exactly five numbered questions, one competency per question, and one preparation tip.
Step 4  Build the LCEL chain prompt | model | StrOutputParser.
Step 5  Run three profiles: beginner data analyst, intermediate Python developer, and beginner AI intern.
Step 6  Check each output against the requested count, focus, and difficulty.
Step 7  Record one prompt revision made after testing and explain why it improved the result.

activities.title: Structured Seven Day Study Plan
activities.document_title: Session 2 Home Task 2 Structured Seven Day Study Plan
activities.overview: Generate a validated seven-day plan with typed daily tasks, time limits, and a final self-check.
activities.primary_output: A study_plan.py program and validated study_plan.json
instructions: Step 1  Define DailyTask with day_number, goal, activity, minutes, and success_check.
Step 2  Define StudyPlan with topic, learner_level, daily_tasks, and final_review_question.
Step 3  Constrain day_number to 1 through 7 and minutes to a reasonable range.
Step 4  Use a prompt template with topic, learner_level, minutes_per_day, and prior_knowledge.
Step 5  Generate a plan and verify locally that there are exactly seven tasks and unique day numbers.
Step 6  Print a compact day-by-day summary and save indented JSON.
Step 7  Test a low time budget and a higher time budget, then compare how task scope changes.
Step 8  Record all local validation checks in validation_notes.txt.

activities.title: Explain Then Quiz Sequential Chain
activities.document_title: Session 3 Class Activity 1 Explain Then Quiz Sequential Chain
activities.overview: Connect two prompt model parser stages so the second stage builds a quiz from the first stage output.
activities.primary_output: A two-stage explain_then_quiz.py LCEL chain
instructions: Step 1  Create an explanation prompt with topic and student_level variables.
Step 2  Build explanation_chain as prompt | model | StrOutputParser.
Step 3  Create a quiz prompt that accepts only an explanation variable and requests three questions plus an answer key.
Step 4  Compose a full chain that maps the explanation output into the quiz prompt.
Step 5  Invoke the explanation chain alone and save its output.
Step 6  Invoke the full chain and save the final quiz.
Step 7  Add print labels showing input, intermediate explanation, and final quiz in chain_trace.txt.
Step 8  Test with embeddings and one nontechnical topic.

activities.title: Parallel Learning Pack and Difficulty Branch
activities.document_title: Session 3 Class Activity 2 Parallel Learning Pack and Difficulty Branch
activities.overview: Run independent chains together and route one request through a beginner or advanced explanation branch.
activities.primary_output: A parallel_and_branching.py workflow
instructions: Step 1  Create summary_chain, analogy_chain, and quiz_chain using separate prompts and one shared model.
Step 2  Place them in RunnableParallel with descriptive output keys.
Step 3  Invoke the parallel runnable for APIs and print each key separately.
Step 4  Create beginner_chain and advanced_chain with clearly different instructions.
Step 5  Build a RunnableBranch whose first condition checks whether level equals beginner and whose default path is advanced_chain.
Step 6  Run the branch once for beginner and once for advanced.
Step 7  Write a table comparing number of executed paths, output shape, and best use case for parallel versus branch.

activities.title: Student Support Request Router
activities.document_title: Session 3 Home Task 1 Student Support Request Router
activities.overview: Build a deterministic LCEL router that sends academic questions, technical errors, and administrative requests to different response chains.
activities.primary_output: A support_router.py application with route tests
instructions: Step 1  Define route_request(text) using simple, documented keyword rules and an unknown fallback.
Step 2  Create three response chains with distinct system behavior: teacher, debugger, and course administrator.
Step 3  Make every chain accept a request key so the same input shape can be reused.
Step 4  Build a RunnableBranch that evaluates the category produced by your router.
Step 5  Create at least nine test messages with three expected categories each plus one ambiguous case.
Step 6  For every test, print expected route, actual route, and whether they match before generating a response.
Step 7  Calculate routing accuracy and describe the ambiguous case.
Step 8  Improve one keyword rule and rerun the same tests.

activities.title: Outline Draft Review Content Pipeline
activities.document_title: Session 3 Home Task 2 Outline Draft Review Content Pipeline
activities.overview: Create a multi-stage writing workflow that produces an outline, drafts from it, and reviews the draft against explicit criteria.
activities.primary_output: A content_pipeline.py workflow with saved stage outputs
instructions: Step 1  Define one input dictionary containing topic, audience, goal, and maximum_words.
Step 2  Build outline_chain and test it independently.
Step 3  Build draft_chain whose prompt receives topic, audience, maximum_words, and outline.
Step 4  Build review_chain whose prompt receives the original goal, word limit, and generated draft.
Step 5  Use RunnablePassthrough.assign or a clear sequence of invoke calls to preserve original inputs.
Step 6  Save every stage output before moving to the next stage.
Step 7  Test the workflow with How vector search helps a study assistant.
Step 8  Read the review and identify one issue, but do not add an automatic revision stage yet.

activities.title: Load Inspect and Compare Documents
activities.document_title: Session 4 Class Activity 1 Load Inspect and Compare Documents
activities.overview: Load a text file and a PDF into LangChain Document objects, then inspect content and metadata before any splitting.
activities.primary_output: A document_loader_lab.py inspection report
instructions: Step 1  Create sample_notes.txt with headings and at least 400 words of course notes.
Step 2  Choose a short PDF of two to five pages that contains selectable text rather than scanned images.
Step 3  Load the text file with TextLoader using UTF-8.
Step 4  Load the PDF with PyPDFLoader and note that each PDF page commonly becomes a separate Document.
Step 5  For every Document, print index, character count, a 120-character preview, and metadata.
Step 6  Create a comparison table covering document count, source metadata, page metadata, and total characters.
Step 7  Rename one source temporarily to trigger FileNotFoundError and add a friendly error message.

activities.title: Chunking Strategy Experiment
activities.document_title: Session 4 Class Activity 2 Chunking Strategy Experiment
activities.overview: Compare three text splitting configurations and judge chunk boundaries, size consistency, and metadata preservation.
activities.primary_output: A chunk_experiment.py report with a recommended configuration
instructions: Step 1  Load sample_notes.txt or a short PDF into LangChain Documents.
Step 2  Test configuration A with chunk_size 300 and overlap 0.
Step 3  Test configuration B with chunk_size 500 and overlap 80.
Step 4  Test configuration C with chunk_size 900 and overlap 150.
Step 5  For each configuration, record chunk count, minimum length, maximum length, and average length.
Step 6  Print the final 100 characters of one chunk and first 100 of the next to inspect a boundary.
Step 7  Verify that source and page metadata survive split_documents.
Step 8  Recommend one configuration for these notes and explain the trade-off, not merely the smallest count.

activities.title: Multi File Course Notes Loader
activities.document_title: Session 4 Home Task 1 Multi File Course Notes Loader
activities.overview: Build a reusable ingestion program that discovers text and PDF files, loads them safely, and normalizes metadata.
activities.primary_output: An ingest_course_notes.py pipeline and ingestion_manifest.json
instructions: Step 1  Create a course_notes folder with unit subfolders and at least five supported files.
Step 2  Use Path.rglob to find .txt and .pdf files recursively.
Step 3  Choose TextLoader for .txt and PyPDFLoader for .pdf.
Step 4  For every returned Document, add source_name, file_type, unit, and ingestion_status metadata.
Step 5  Catch errors per file so one corrupted file does not stop the entire run.
Step 6  Create a manifest with file path, status, number of returned documents, characters, and error message if any.
Step 7  Detect duplicate file names and warn even when their paths differ.
Step 8  Print totals for discovered files, successful files, failed files, and produced Documents.

activities.title: Chunk Quality Auditor
activities.document_title: Session 4 Home Task 2 Chunk Quality Auditor
activities.overview: Create deterministic checks that flag tiny chunks, oversized chunks, missing metadata, and suspicious boundaries.
activities.primary_output: A chunk_auditor.py program and chunk_audit.csv
instructions: Step 1  Load and split at least two source files with one documented chunk size and overlap.
Step 2  Assign a stable chunk_id and retain source and page metadata.
Step 3  Calculate character count, word count, starts_mid_sentence, ends_mid_sentence, and metadata_complete.
Step 4  Flag chunks below 120 characters or above the configured chunk size plus a small tolerance.
Step 5  Flag chunks missing a source value and chunks that contain mostly whitespace.
Step 6  Write one CSV row per chunk with flags joined into a readable field.
Step 7  Print counts and percentages for every flag type.
Step 8  Manually inspect five flagged chunks and classify each warning as useful or false positive.

activities.title: Semantic Search over Study Notes
activities.document_title: Session 5 Class Activity 1 Semantic Search over Study Notes
activities.overview: Embed a small set of note cards in an in-memory vector store and retrieve meaningfully related content.
activities.primary_output: A semantic_search_lab.py program with ranked results
instructions: Step 1  Create eight Document objects covering APIs, prompts, messages, chains, loaders, chunks, embeddings, and retrievers.
Step 2  Give each Document a unique note_id and topic in metadata.
Step 3  Create GoogleGenerativeAIEmbeddings using GEMINI_EMBEDDING_MODEL from .env.
Step 4  Index the Documents in InMemoryVectorStore.
Step 5  Search for How can an app find related text even when the words differ and return the top three.
Step 6  Print rank, note_id, topic, score if available, and page content.
Step 7  Run a simple keyword search over the same notes and compare the results.
Step 8  Repeat with two additional queries and record one semantic match that keyword search missed.

activities.title: Retriever Tuning Challenge
activities.document_title: Session 5 Class Activity 2 Retriever Tuning Challenge
activities.overview: Compare top k values and chunking settings against a small set of questions with expected source IDs.
activities.primary_output: A retriever_tuning.py comparison and recommendation
instructions: Step 1  Create six test cases, each containing query and expected_note_ids.
Step 2  For k values 1, 2, and 4, create a retriever with search_kwargs={'k': k}.
Step 3  Invoke the retriever for every query and collect returned note IDs.
Step 4  Mark a test as a hit when at least one expected ID is retrieved.
Step 5  Manually label every returned result relevant or not relevant for one selected k.
Step 6  Calculate hit rate for all k values and irrelevant-result count for the manually reviewed setting.
Step 7  Choose a recommended k and explain its coverage and noise trade-off.
Step 8  Repeat one query after rewriting it as a paraphrase and note whether the same source remains retrievable.

activities.title: Course FAQ Semantic Search
activities.document_title: Session 5 Home Task 1 Course FAQ Semantic Search
activities.overview: Create a searchable FAQ knowledge base with source labels, query logging, and a no confident match message.
activities.primary_output: An faq_search.py application with at least 15 FAQ entries
instructions: Step 1  Write at least 15 original FAQ entries with faq_id, topic, question, answer, and source_label.
Step 2  Load the JSON and convert each entry into a Document whose page_content combines question and answer.
Step 3  Store all remaining fields in metadata.
Step 4  Index the corpus with Gemini embeddings and InMemoryVectorStore.
Step 5  Accept repeated user queries until exit is entered.
Step 6  Display the top three stored answers with FAQ ID and source label.
Step 7  Provide a cautious message when the user marks all three results irrelevant; do not ask Gemini to invent an answer.
Step 8  Append timestamp-free query text and returned IDs to query_log.jsonl, avoiding personal information.
Step 9  Test ten queries including paraphrases, ambiguous wording, and two out-of-scope questions.

activities.title: Retrieval Evaluation with Hit at K
activities.document_title: Session 5 Home Task 2 Retrieval Evaluation with Hit at K
activities.overview: Build a labeled test set, calculate hit at k, inspect failures, and compare two retrieval configurations.
activities.primary_output: A retrieval_eval.py harness and evaluation report
instructions: Step 1  Create at least 12 tests with query, expected_ids, category, and difficulty.
Step 2  Freeze the test file before running the baseline so expectations are not changed to match results.
Step 3  For every query, retrieve the top three IDs and record their ranks.
Step 4  Calculate Hit at 1 and Hit at 3 overall and by category.
Step 5  Print every miss with the returned text previews for diagnosis.
Step 6  Change exactly one configuration variable and rebuild the index.
Step 7  Run the same test set again and calculate the same metrics.
Step 8  Report which queries improved, regressed, or stayed the same.
Step 9  State whether the change should be kept and mention at least one metric limitation.

activities.title: Grounded Notes Question Answering
activities.document_title: Session 6 Class Activity 1 Grounded Notes Question Answering
activities.overview: Connect retrieval to Gemini and require answers to use only supplied context with visible source labels.
activities.primary_output: A grounded_qa.py RAG workflow
instructions: Step 1  Create or reuse a retriever that returns three Documents.
Step 2  Write format_context to join content and metadata into labeled context blocks.
Step 3  Create a system prompt that prohibits unsupported claims and defines the exact fallback sentence.
Step 4  Create a human prompt with CONTEXT and QUESTION sections.
Step 5  Retrieve documents, format context, invoke the chain, and print both retrieved IDs and final answer.
Step 6  Test two answerable questions, one partially answerable question, and two out-of-scope questions.
Step 7  For each answer, manually mark grounded, partially grounded, or unsupported and explain the label.
Step 8  Revise one prompt instruction if the model answers an out-of-scope question anyway.

activities.title: Safe Calculator Tool Call
activities.document_title: Session 6 Class Activity 2 Safe Calculator Tool Call
activities.overview: Define one narrow Python tool, let Gemini request it, execute the call, and return the result for a final response.
activities.primary_output: A safe_tool_call.py program with a visible tool trace
instructions: Step 1  Define calculate_total with typed numeric arguments and a docstring describing when to use it.
Step 2  Validate quantity, price, and discount range inside the Python function.
Step 3  Bind only this tool to the model.
Step 4  Send a user request that requires calculation and inspect ai_message.tool_calls before execution.
Step 5  Reject any unrecognized tool name rather than executing it dynamically.
Step 6  Invoke calculate_total with the tool-call object and append the returned ToolMessage.
Step 7  Call the bound model again with human message, AI tool request, and tool result.
Step 8  Test a valid request, a no-tool conceptual question, and an invalid negative quantity.

activities.title: Document Assistant with Verified Citations
activities.document_title: Session 6 Home Task 1 Document Assistant with Verified Citations
activities.overview: Build a small RAG assistant that validates cited source IDs and records evidence for every test question.
activities.primary_output: A document_assistant.py application with eight test records
instructions: Step 1  Load the source, normalize source and page metadata, and split it using a documented configuration.
Step 2  Assign a stable chunk_id to every chunk before indexing.
Step 3  Build an InMemoryVectorStore with Gemini embeddings and a top-three retriever.
Step 4  Define a Pydantic AnswerWithSources schema containing answer, source_ids, and sufficient_context.
Step 5  Prompt Gemini to use only formatted chunks and return the schema.
Step 6  After generation, reject any source_id not present among the retrieved chunk IDs.
Step 7  Create eight tests: four answerable, two paraphrased, and two unanswerable.
Step 8  Store question, retrieved IDs, structured answer, citation_valid, and manual_grounding_label for every test.
Step 9  Write setup, architecture, usage, limitations, and privacy notes in README.md.

activities.title: Two Tool Study Agent
activities.document_title: Session 6 Home Task 2 Two Tool Study Agent
activities.overview: Build a bounded agent that chooses between a glossary lookup and a grade calculator, then test tool choice and arguments.
activities.primary_output: A study_agent.py program with a tool-use evaluation table
instructions: Step 1  Create glossary_lookup(term) that returns a stored definition or a clear not-found result.
Step 2  Create calculate_weighted_grade(scores, weights) with length, range, and total-weight validation.
Step 3  Use clear @tool docstrings that distinguish when each tool should be selected.
Step 4  Create an agent with create_agent using the Gemini model and the two tools.
Step 5  Write at least ten tests: four glossary, three grade calculations, two no-tool questions, and one ambiguous request.
Step 6  For every test, record expected tool, actual tool, arguments, final answer, and pass or fail.
Step 7  Check that the agent stops and does not call a tool repeatedly without progress.
Step 8  Revise one tool description after observing a failure and rerun the identical tests.
Step 9  Add a limitations section describing unsupported and unsafe actions.

activities.title: Repair a Broken Prompt Chain
activities.document_title: Session 7 Class Activity 1 Repair a Broken Prompt Chain
activities.overview: Use error messages, type inspection, and stage isolation to fix five intentional defects in one LangChain program.
activities.primary_output: A repaired_chain.py file and debugging log
instructions: Step 1  Run the starter exactly once and capture the first traceback or unexpected behavior.
Step 2  Create a debugging table with symptom, suspected stage, experiment, result, root cause, and fix.
Step 3  Inspect prompt.input_variables and compare them with the invoke dictionary.
Step 4  Invoke the prompt alone and print its type and formatted messages.
Step 5  Invoke the model on the formatted prompt and inspect the returned type.
Step 6  Repair only the currently evidenced defect, rerun, and continue until all five are fixed.
Step 7  Add one assertion checking that the final value is a nonempty string.
Step 8  Run two topics after repair to confirm the chain is reusable.

activities.title: Diagnose a Failing RAG Answer
activities.document_title: Session 7 Class Activity 2 Diagnose a Failing RAG Answer
activities.overview: Inspect retrieval and generation separately to determine why a document question receives a weak or unsupported answer.
activities.primary_output: A rag_diagnosis.md evidence report and improved configuration
instructions: Step 1  Run the five provided questions and save baseline question, expected source, retrieved IDs, context, and answer.
Step 2  For each failure, check whether the expected source exists in the loaded corpus.
Step 3  Check whether the expected source became a chunk and retained its ID.
Step 4  Check whether that chunk appears in the top-k results.
Step 5  If retrieved, verify that format_context included its full relevant passage.
Step 6  If context is correct, inspect the grounding and fallback instructions in the prompt.
Step 7  Assign one primary failure category and cite evidence.
Step 8  Change one parameter or code defect, rerun all five questions, and compare baseline with fixed results.

activities.title: Four Case Debugging Challenge Pack
activities.document_title: Session 7 Home Task 1 Four Case Debugging Challenge Pack
activities.overview: Repair environment, prompt, schema, and retrieval failures and explain the diagnostic evidence for each.
activities.primary_output: Four repaired programs and a consolidated debug report
instructions: Step 1  Case 1: record Python executable, pip executable, package location, and failed import before fixing the environment mismatch.
Step 2  Case 2: inspect prompt.input_variables and invocation keys; repair only mismatched names.
Step 3  Case 3: capture the validation error, identify the invalid field, and revise either schema or prompt based on the intended contract.
Step 4  Case 4: print corpus IDs, chunks, query, and ranked results; repair one indexing or retrieval configuration issue.
Step 5  For every case, write reproduce, observe, hypothesize, test, fix, and verify sections.
Step 6  Add at least one automated assertion or deterministic check per case.
Step 7  Run all cases from a fresh terminal after repairs.
Step 8  Create summary.md comparing which diagnostic method was most useful in each category.

activities.title: Regression Test Harness for a LangChain Application
activities.document_title: Session 7 Home Task 2 Regression Test Harness for a LangChain Application
activities.overview: Create repeatable tests that catch changes in output structure, routing, retrieval, and refusal behavior.
activities.primary_output: A regression_tests.py harness and test summary
instructions: Step 1  List the application's promised behaviors and mark each deterministic or model-dependent.
Step 2  Create at least ten labeled tests, including normal, edge, and out-of-scope inputs.
Step 3  Implement deterministic checks such as type, nonempty value, valid schema, route, citation subset, or exact fallback when required.
Step 4  For model-dependent quality, use simple rubric fields and manual review rather than exact string equality.
Step 5  Run the baseline and store input, output evidence, pass or fail, error, and elapsed seconds.
Step 6  Make one small prompt or retrieval change.
Step 7  Rerun the identical tests and compare passes, failures, new errors, and latency.
Step 8  Restore or revise the change if it creates an important regression.
Step 9  Document which tests are stable enough for automation and which still need human judgment.

activities.title: Capstone Readiness Review
activities.document_title: Session 8 Class Activity 1 Capstone Readiness Review
activities.overview: Run a structured peer review of setup, functionality, grounding, safety, testing, and explanation before the showcase.
activities.primary_output: A completed readiness review and prioritized fix list
instructions: Step 1  State the project's user, problem, expected input, expected output, and success criteria in under one minute.
Step 2  Verify that README setup instructions identify Python version, installation, environment variables, and run command.
Step 3  Check that .env is absent and .env.example contains placeholders only.
Step 4  Run one normal case, one edge case, one out-of-scope case, and one intentional failure case.
Step 5  For RAG, inspect retrieved sources and citations; for tools, inspect selected tool and arguments; for chains, inspect intermediate stages.
Step 6  Record actual behavior, evidence, severity, and recommended fix for every failed check.
Step 7  Classify findings as blocker, important, or optional.
Step 8  Select at most three fixes that can realistically be completed before the showcase.

activities.title: Four Minute Demo Rehearsal
activities.document_title: Session 8 Class Activity 2 Four Minute Demo Rehearsal
activities.overview: Practice a concise technical demonstration and use observer feedback to improve clarity, timing, and recovery from one failure.
activities.primary_output: A timed demo script and peer feedback record
instructions: Step 1  Write a four-part script: problem and user, architecture, live success, limitation and learning.
Step 2  Allocate approximately 30 seconds, 45 seconds, 105 seconds, and 60 seconds to the four parts, leaving time for transitions.
Step 3  Show the exact input, visible output, and evidence such as sources, tool call, or intermediate stage.
Step 4  Demonstrate one controlled failure, refusal, or known limitation without exposing secrets.
Step 5  Use the backup artifact if the API fails rather than spending the full presentation debugging.
Step 6  Collect timer notes and observer answers to four comprehension questions.
Step 7  Revise the script by removing or simplifying at least one confusing section.
Step 8  Deliver the second rehearsal and record whether timing and clarity improved.

activities.title: Final Project Packaging
activities.document_title: Session 8 Home Task 1 Final Project Packaging
activities.overview: Prepare a clean and reproducible capstone submission with setup instructions, dependency versions, sample data, tests, and secret-safe configuration.
activities.primary_output: A submission-ready capstone folder
instructions: Step 1  Remove temporary outputs, __pycache__, personal paths, unused files, and duplicate scripts.
Step 2  Move secrets to .env and create .env.example with variable names and placeholder values only.
Step 3  Create .gitignore covering .env, caches, virtual environments if any, and generated private outputs.
Step 4  Write README sections for overview, intended user, features, architecture, setup, run command, sample use, tests, limitations, safety, and project structure.
Step 5  Create a minimal requirements.txt containing only packages the project imports.
Step 6  Provide small nonconfidential sample data or instructions for creating it.
Step 7  Run at least five final tests and save a human-readable result summary.
Step 8  Copy the project to a new folder or use a fresh terminal and follow the README exactly.
Step 9  Create final_submission.zip and open it once to confirm the expected files are present.

activities.title: Capstone Reflection and Next Version Plan
activities.document_title: Session 8 Home Task 2 Capstone Reflection and Next Version Plan
activities.overview: Use test evidence and project experience to explain design decisions, limitations, and a realistic next development milestone.
activities.primary_output: A two to three page capstone reflection
instructions: Step 1  Write a short problem statement naming the intended user and the task the project supports.
Step 2  Describe the architecture from input to output and justify the major LangChain components chosen.
Step 3  Summarize the test set and report at least two quantitative results such as pass count, retrieval hit rate, valid-citation rate, tool-choice accuracy, or refusal success.

Step 3  Summarize automated pass count, end-to-end outcomes, route distribution, stop reasons, call counts, and observed latency ranges where available.

Step 5  Explain the root cause and current mitigation for each failure.
Step 6  Describe privacy, safety, cost, and reliability limitations honestly.
Step 7  Create at least eight backlog items with user value, risk reduction, effort, dependency, and acceptance test.
Step 8  Prioritize only three items for the next version and justify why the rest wait.
Step 9  Write a two-week implementation sequence for the three priorities without promising production readiness.
Step 10  End with one specific technical skill to study next and one experiment to run.

activities.title: Define Quality and Build a Failure Taxonomy
activities.document_title: Session 1 Class Activity 1 Define Quality and Build a Failure Taxonomy
activities.overview: Turn a vague claim that an AI answer is good into observable criteria and named failure types.
activities.primary_output: A quality contract and failure taxonomy
instructions: Step 1  Write one sentence naming the user, task, and useful outcome.
Step 2  List four behaviors that must occur and four behaviors that must never occur.
Step 3  Define at least six quality criteria with a measurable pass condition for each one.
Step 4  Separate criteria into content, instruction following, safety, and operations.
Step 5  Create at least eight failure labels such as incorrect fact, missing requirement, unsupported claim, empty output, scope drift, or excessive latency.
Step 6  Write one positive and one failing example for each of four important failure labels.
Step 7  Rate each failure as low, medium, or high impact and explain the highest two ratings.
Step 8  Exchange the contract with a partner and identify one criterion that two reviewers could interpret differently.
Step 9  Rewrite that criterion so two reviewers are more likely to agree.

activities.title: Build Your First Deterministic Evaluation Harness
activities.document_title: Session 1 Class Activity 2 Build Your First Deterministic Evaluation Harness
activities.overview: Run repeatable Python checks and summarize results without calling a model.
activities.primary_output: A working eval_harness.py and result table
instructions: Step 1  Run the starter code and predict the result for both supplied cases before viewing output.
Step 2  Add three cases containing one strong answer, one overlong answer, and one answer missing a required term.
Step 3  Add a failure_labels list to every result and populate it from failed checks.
Step 4  Calculate passed case count, total case count, and pass rate.
Step 5  Print one row per case with case ID, individual checks, final result, and failure labels.
Step 6  Add assertions for the expected result of all five cases.
Step 7  Change one threshold intentionally and record which cases change result.
Step 8  Restore the correct threshold and write two quality criteria that this harness cannot judge reliably.

activities.title: Create a Balanced Evaluation Dataset
activities.document_title: Session 1 Home Task 1 Create a Balanced Evaluation Dataset
activities.overview: Build a 20-case dataset that represents normal use, boundaries, failures, and safety behavior.
activities.primary_output: A validated JSONL dataset and dataset card
instructions: Step 1  Define a row schema containing case_id, category, question, student_level, must_include, must_avoid, maximum_words, expected_behavior, and severity.
Step 2  Write eight ordinary cases across at least four technical topics.
Step 3  Write four boundary cases involving blank input, long input, unusual wording, or a strict length limit.
Step 4  Write four instruction-following cases with different audience and output requirements.
Step 5  Write four safety or scope cases that should be refused, redirected, or handled cautiously.
Step 6  Avoid duplicate questions that test the same wording and behavior.
Step 7  Write validate_dataset.py to check unique IDs, allowed category values, required fields, positive limits, and exactly 20 rows.
Step 8  Run validation, fix every error, and record the final category counts.
Step 9  Write a dataset card covering purpose, intended use, case distribution, important gaps, and the rule for adding new cases.

activities.title: Write an Application Evaluation Plan
activities.document_title: Session 1 Home Task 2 Write an Application Evaluation Plan
activities.overview: Connect quality criteria, evaluators, datasets, risks, and release decisions in one practical plan.
activities.primary_output: An evaluation plan and risk register
instructions: Step 1  Describe the application input, output, user, boundary, and one explicit non-goal.
Step 2  Create three layers named component checks, complete application checks, and operational checks.
Step 3  Map every quality criterion to a dataset slice, evaluator, metric, passing threshold, and failure action.
Step 4  Choose which checks run on every code change, before a class demo, and only during a deeper review.
Step 5  Define at least three release blockers, including one safety blocker.
Step 6  Set a small call budget and explain how deterministic checks reduce unnecessary Gemini calls.
Step 7  Create a risk register with likelihood, impact, detection method, mitigation, owner, and remaining risk.
Step 8  Include evaluator risks such as ambiguous rubrics, judge inconsistency, and an unrepresentative dataset.
Step 9  Walk through one failed case from detection to decision and corrective action.

activities.title: Design and Calibrate a Scoring Rubric
activities.document_title: Session 2 Class Activity 1 Design and Calibrate a Scoring Rubric
activities.overview: Write score levels that two reviewers can apply to the same answer with similar results.
activities.primary_output: A calibrated five point rubric and review notes
instructions: Step 1  Write a one-sentence evaluation goal and identify the intended student level.
Step 2  Define four criteria and assign a weight or state that all are equally important.
Step 3  Describe score 1, score 3, and score 5 for every criterion using observable evidence.
Step 4  Write or use six sample answers that include excellent, partial, verbose, misleading, and unrelated cases.
Step 5  Score all six independently before discussing them with a partner.
Step 6  Compare total scores and criterion scores, then calculate exact agreement count.
Step 7  Discuss the two largest disagreements and identify the wording that allowed both interpretations.
Step 8  Revise the rubric and rescore only the disagreement cases.
Step 9  Set a passing rule and one critical-failure override for incorrect information.

activities.title: Choose the Right Evaluation Method
activities.document_title: Session 2 Class Activity 2 Choose the Right Evaluation Method
activities.overview: Compare code checks, human review, gold answer checks, and Gemini judging on the same cases.
activities.primary_output: A method comparison matrix and hybrid evaluator design
instructions: Step 1  For each scenario, identify the decision the evaluation must support.
Step 2  Mark whether a deterministic code check can answer the question completely or only partially.
Step 3  Choose a gold-answer comparison when a trusted expected answer exists and wording variation can be handled fairly.
Step 4  Choose human review when context, consequences, or ambiguity require accountable judgment.
Step 5  Choose Gemini judging only when the rubric and input provide enough evidence for a bounded decision.
Step 6  Rate every chosen method for repeatability, speed, cost, and risk of false confidence.
Step 7  Design a pipeline that runs code checks first, then selects only eligible cases for judging or human review.
Step 8  Add an escalation rule for judge uncertainty or conflict with a critical deterministic check.

activities.title: Build a Structured Gemini Judge
activities.document_title: Session 2 Home Task 1 Build a Structured Gemini Judge
activities.overview: Use a clear rubric and Pydantic schema to return machine-checkable evaluation results.
activities.primary_output: A judge.py program and ten judged cases
instructions: Step 1  Run the starter once and inspect the returned Pydantic object and model_dump output.
Step 2  Move the rubric into a named constant so every case uses identical scoring instructions.
Step 3  Add case_id and criterion_scores to the output schema while keeping each score between 1 and 5.
Step 4  Calculate the final pass value in Python from the validated scores and critical-failure flags.
Step 5  Create ten cases containing strong, partial, incorrect, verbose, irrelevant, and instruction-like answer text.
Step 6  Ensure the prompt tells the judge to treat candidate text as data rather than new instructions.
Step 7  Catch validation or API errors and record a failed_eval status instead of inventing a score.
Step 8  Write one JSONL result per case without storing the API key or environment contents.
Step 9  Manually inspect all failed cases and any result whose reason does not match its scores.

activities.title: Audit Judge Agreement and Bias
activities.document_title: Session 2 Home Task 2 Audit Judge Agreement and Bias
activities.overview: Compare Gemini judgments with human labels and inspect patterns behind disagreements.
activities.primary_output: A calibrated judge audit and revised rubric
instructions: Step 1  Select 12 cases covering clear passes, clear failures, and at least four borderline answers.
Step 2  Have two reviewers score each case independently with the same rubric.
Step 3  Resolve human disagreement through discussion and preserve both original scores.
Step 4  Run the Gemini judge once per case with temperature zero.
Step 5  Calculate exact pass agreement, average absolute score difference, false pass count, and false fail count.
Step 6  Create two meaning-preserving pairs that change only polish or length and compare judge scores.
Step 7  Shuffle case order, rerun four selected cases, and record any changed results.
Step 8  Group disagreements by failure type and identify whether the rubric, data, or judge behavior is the likely cause.
Step 9  Revise one rubric statement or add one escalation condition, then rerun only affected cases.
Step 10  State the limited decisions for which this judge is acceptable and the decisions that still require a person.

activities.title: Run an Offline Prompt Comparison
activities.document_title: Session 3 Class Activity 1 Run an Offline Prompt Comparison
activities.overview: Evaluate two prompt configurations on the same fixed cases and make a result based choice.
activities.primary_output: A prompt comparison script and case level results
instructions: Step 1  Run the starter and verify that every case is evaluated under prompt A and prompt B.
Step 2  Save configuration name, case ID, generated answer, check results, and score for every run.
Step 3  Add three cases that test a strict word limit, an advanced audience, and an answer that should admit missing information.
Step 4  Keep model name, temperature, case set, and evaluator unchanged during the comparison.
Step 5  Calculate mean score, pass rate, word-limit pass rate, and required-concept pass rate for each prompt.
Step 6  Create a paired table showing the score change for every case.
Step 7  Mark any high-severity case that regresses even if the candidate average improves.
Step 8  Choose keep baseline, adopt candidate, or gather more evidence and justify the decision.

activities.title: Interpret Benchmarks and Leaderboards Carefully
activities.document_title: Session 3 Class Activity 2 Interpret Benchmarks and Leaderboards Carefully
activities.overview: Use a supplied candidate table without confusing benchmark rank with application suitability.
activities.primary_output: A model selection memo and benchmark risk checklist
instructions: Step 1  Read the user requirement and list the three capabilities that matter most for the study assistant.
Step 2  Identify which table columns provide direct evidence, indirect evidence, or no evidence for each capability.
Step 3  Normalize the supplied metrics to a common 0 to 100 scale only where that transformation makes sense.
Step 4  Create weights before calculating a weighted score and explain every weight.
Step 5  Check whether two candidates are practically tied when score differences are small.
Step 6  Describe how benchmark saturation can make top scores hard to distinguish.
Step 7  Describe how exposure to test items can make a benchmark score look stronger than unseen performance.
Step 8  Apply latency and usage limits as constraints rather than treating them as optional notes.
Step 9  Select one candidate for a small application-specific trial and list five cases required before final adoption.

activities.title: Measure Stability Across Repeated Trials
activities.document_title: Session 3 Home Task 1 Measure Stability Across Repeated Trials
activities.overview: Repeat selected cases and quantify how often outputs or scores change.
activities.primary_output: A stability experiment and variance report
instructions: Step 1  Choose two clear cases and three borderline or instruction-sensitive cases.
Step 2  Define configuration A with temperature zero and configuration B with a modest nonzero temperature.
Step 3  Run every case three times under each configuration and save all 30 generated answers.
Step 4  Assign a unique run ID and preserve case ID, configuration, trial number, and answer.
Step 5  Apply deterministic checks to all saved answers before using the judge.
Step 6  Judge the saved answers with one unchanged rubric and record failures separately from scores.
Step 7  For every case and configuration, calculate pass consistency, minimum score, maximum score, and score range.
Step 8  Manually compare repeated answers when the score range is two or more points.
Step 9  Rerun the judge on three unchanged answers to test judge stability separately.
Step 10  Recommend a configuration and identify cases that still require a larger sample or human review.

activities.title: Build a Constrained Model Selection Scorecard
activities.document_title: Session 3 Home Task 2 Build a Constrained Model Selection Scorecard
activities.overview: Combine application quality, safety, stability, latency, and call usage in a defensible selection process.
activities.primary_output: A candidate scorecard and selection decision
instructions: Step 1  Define required metrics for quality pass rate, high-severity failure count, stability, median latency, and average model calls.
Step 2  Set hard gates for safety and high-severity failures before assigning weights.
Step 3  Create a CSV with one row per candidate and include the source run ID for every aggregated value.
Step 4  Normalize preference metrics so higher values consistently mean better results.
Step 5  Choose weights that total 100 percent and write the reason for each weight before calculating results.
Step 6  Remove candidates that fail a hard gate, then calculate weighted scores for the remaining candidates.
Step 7  Read at least three failed cases from the apparent winner before recommending it.
Step 8  Increase and decrease the largest weight by ten points while adjusting another weight to keep the total fixed.
Step 9  Set a primary choice, fallback choice, and one condition that would reopen the decision.

activities.title: Calculate Retrieval Metrics
activities.document_title: Session 4 Class Activity 1 Calculate Retrieval Metrics
activities.overview: Measure whether relevant chunks appear and how early they are ranked.
activities.primary_output: A retrieval metrics script and hand checked worksheet
instructions: Step 1  Read the first sample and calculate hit at 3, reciprocal rank, and precision at 3 by hand.
Step 2  Run the starter and compare code output with the hand calculation.
Step 3  Add five sample queries including no hit, first-rank hit, multiple relevant hits, and a relevant result beyond k.
Step 4  Calculate query-level metrics for all six samples.
Step 5  Calculate overall hit rate at 1, hit rate at 3, mean reciprocal rank, and mean precision at 3.
Step 6  Add assertions for three cases whose results are easy to verify manually.
Step 7  Write one sentence interpreting each aggregate metric in this dataset.
Step 8  Identify a query where hit at 3 looks successful but precision at 3 reveals distracting results.

activities.title: Compare Top K and Chunking Settings
activities.document_title: Session 4 Class Activity 2 Compare Top K and Chunking Settings
activities.overview: Change one retrieval setting at a time and inspect both metrics and retrieved text.
activities.primary_output: A controlled retrieval experiment
instructions: Step 1  Run the starter retriever and describe its token-overlap scoring rule.
Step 2  Create five questions and label the chunk IDs that contain enough information to answer each one.
Step 3  Build version S with one idea per small chunk and version L with two or more related ideas per larger chunk.
Step 4  Run every question against both versions at k values 1, 2, and 3.
Step 5  Calculate hit rate, mean reciprocal rank, and average retrieved word count for every setting.
Step 6  Inspect all cases where increasing k adds irrelevant context without changing hit result.
Step 7  Inspect all cases where a small chunk loses information needed to answer fully.
Step 8  Choose one setting for a generator limited to 180 context words and justify the tradeoff.

activities.title: Build a Retrieval Evaluation Bench
activities.document_title: Session 4 Home Task 1 Build a Retrieval Evaluation Bench
activities.overview: Create a 20-query benchmark that measures retrieval quality before any answer is generated.
activities.primary_output: A reusable retrieval bench and result report
instructions: Step 1  Create a stable chunk collection and record chunk ID, source label, section, and text.
Step 2  Write 20 queries with category, relevant chunk IDs, and answerable true or false.
Step 3  Have a second person review at least five relevance labels before running the benchmark.
Step 4  Record retriever name, tokenization or embedding approach, chunk version, k, and run ID.
Step 5  Save ranked IDs and scores for every query before calculating aggregate results.
Step 6  Calculate hit rate at 1 and 3, mean reciprocal rank, precision at 3, and no-result accuracy for unanswerable cases.
Step 7  Break metrics down by direct, paraphrase, multi-part, ambiguous, and unanswerable categories.
Step 8  Inspect every miss and label the likely cause as labeling, wording, chunking, ranking, or missing content.
Step 9  Choose the five highest-value failures and propose one precise change for each.
Step 10  Rerun two corrected labels only when evidence shows the original label was wrong; preserve the initial result record.

activities.title: Diagnose Retrieval Failures and Improve One Variable
activities.document_title: Session 4 Home Task 2 Diagnose Retrieval Failures and Improve One Variable
activities.overview: Use failure evidence to choose one retrieval change and verify its effect without moving the goalposts.
activities.primary_output: A baseline improvement comparison and diagnosis log
instructions: Step 1  Freeze the baseline dataset, labels, metric functions, and run configuration file.
Step 2  Group baseline misses and select one pattern with at least three affected cases.
Step 3  Write a hypothesis naming the change, expected affected cases, expected metric movement, and possible regression.
Step 4  Choose one change such as stop-word removal, chunk overlap, query rewriting, score threshold, or k.
Step 5  Implement the change under a new configuration name without overwriting the baseline code or results.
Step 6  Run the identical 20 cases and save ranked outputs with a new run ID.
Step 7  Create a paired table showing rank movement for the first relevant result in every case.
Step 8  Report changed aggregate and category metrics, improved cases, unchanged cases, and regressions.
Step 9  Inspect at least three improvements and every regression manually.
Step 10  Choose keep, reject, or modify the change using the hypothesis and release rule.

activities.title: Trace the RAG Quality Triad
activities.document_title: Session 5 Class Activity 1 Trace the RAG Quality Triad
activities.overview: Judge retrieved context grounded answer content and question relevance as separate signals.
activities.primary_output: A completed RAG case analysis matrix
instructions: Step 1  Write one plain-language definition and one counterexample for each of the three criteria.
Step 2  Read each question and context before reading the answer so retrieval usefulness is judged independently.
Step 3  Score context relevance from 1 to 5 and quote a short evidence phrase from the supplied context in your notes.
Step 4  List each factual claim in the answer and mark supported, contradicted, or not present in context.
Step 5  Score groundedness based on the claim markings rather than writing quality.
Step 6  Score answer relevance by checking whether the actual question and requested format were addressed.
Step 7  Assign a primary cause label of retrieval, generation, both, or no failure.
Step 8  Choose the next diagnostic action for each failed case.
Step 9  Compare two cases that receive the same total score for different reasons and explain why the response should differ.

activities.title: Build a Structured RAG Answer Judge
activities.document_title: Session 5 Class Activity 2 Build a Structured RAG Answer Judge
activities.overview: Return separate triad scores and an unsupported claim finding from Gemini.
activities.primary_output: A rag_judge.py program and comparison notes
instructions: Step 1  Copy the starter and run one clear case to inspect the RagScore object.
Step 2  Add case_id, judge_status, and needs_human_review fields to the saved result record.
Step 3  Write local code that fails any case with groundedness below 4 even if the other scores are high.
Step 4  Add an escalation rule when any score is 3 or the explanation conflicts with the numeric scores.
Step 5  Run the four selected cases with an unchanged prompt and temperature zero.
Step 6  Compare every Gemini score with the earlier human score and record the absolute difference.
Step 7  Inspect the unsupported_claim field and replace empty or vague findings only by improving the prompt, never by editing results.
Step 8  Record schema or API failure as judge_status failed_eval without creating substitute scores.
Step 9  Write a short conclusion about which cases this judge handles reliably and which remain ambiguous.

activities.title: Evaluate a Complete RAG Pipeline
activities.document_title: Session 5 Home Task 1 Evaluate a Complete RAG Pipeline
activities.overview: Measure retrieval and answer behavior together while preserving enough evidence to locate failures.
activities.primary_output: A 20-case full pipeline evaluation report
instructions: Step 1  Freeze a run configuration containing dataset version, chunk version, retriever settings, prompt version, judge rubric version, and model name.
Step 2  For each case, save ranked chunk IDs, scores, selected context text, generated answer, call count, and elapsed time.
Step 3  Run deterministic checks for empty answer, requested format, maximum words, and expected abstention behavior.
Step 4  Calculate retrieval hit at 3 and reciprocal rank for answerable cases.
Step 5  Apply the structured RAG judge and local groundedness gate to successful generations.
Step 6  Label the primary outcome as pass, retrieval_failure, generation_failure, both_failed, correct_abstention, or eval_error.
Step 7  Calculate end-to-end pass rate, groundedness gate rate, correct abstention rate, and median latency.
Step 8  Break results down by direct, paraphrase, multi-part, ambiguous, and unanswerable categories.
Step 9  Inspect every unsupported claim and the five slowest cases.
Step 10  Select the three most important failure patterns and propose one next experiment for each.

activities.title: Calibrate a RAG Judge with Human Claim Labels
activities.document_title: Session 5 Home Task 2 Calibrate a RAG Judge with Human Claim Labels
activities.overview: Compare automated groundedness judgments with claim by claim human analysis.
activities.primary_output: A RAG judge calibration report and final use policy
instructions: Step 1  Split each answer into atomic factual claims and assign stable claim IDs.
Step 2  For every claim, mark supported, contradicted, or absent from context and add a short context evidence phrase.
Step 3  Have two reviewers label five difficult cases independently and resolve disagreements.
Step 4  Define the human case result as pass only when no factual claim is contradicted or absent.
Step 5  Run the RAG judge on all 15 saved triples without changing the rubric between cases.
Step 6  Convert the judge groundedness result into pass or fail using the local gate.
Step 7  Calculate exact case agreement, unsupported-case false pass rate, supported-case false fail rate, and average score difference.
Step 8  Inspect every false pass first and identify the claim pattern the judge missed.
Step 9  Test one prompt or schema improvement on only the disagreement set.
Step 10  Write the final policy for automatic pass, automatic fail, and human escalation.

activities.title: Test Agent Routes Tools and Stop Rules
activities.document_title: Session 6 Class Activity 1 Test Agent Routes Tools and Stop Rules
activities.overview: Evaluate an agent trace as structured behavior instead of judging only its final message.
activities.primary_output: An agent behavior test harness and trace report
instructions: Step 1  Run the starter with the supplied case and trace, then explain each boolean check.
Step 2  Extend AgentCase with expected status, maximum tool calls, and approval required.
Step 3  Extend the trace schema with tool arguments, tool call count, approval event, and final response.
Step 4  Write checks for route, tool, argument schema, step limit, tool-call limit, terminal status, and approval presence.
Step 5  Create ten cases containing at least three successful, two wrong-route, two invalid-argument, one loop-limit, one missing-approval, and one failed-status example.
Step 6  Calculate pass rate for each individual check and complete-case pass rate.
Step 7  Find one trace with a convincing final answer that still fails process checks.
Step 8  Assign a primary failure label and recommended fix for every failed case.

activities.title: Run a Safety Probe Lab
activities.document_title: Session 6 Class Activity 2 Run a Safety Probe Lab
activities.overview: Test leakage scope drift harmful tone and unauthorized action behavior with expected safe outcomes.
activities.primary_output: A safety probe set and failure analysis
instructions: Step 1  Define four category-specific pass conditions before writing probe text.
Step 2  Create three probes per category for a total of 12 cases.
Step 3  Use a fake token such as DEMO_SECRET_7391 and confirm no submitted file contains a real key.
Step 4  For each probe, record expected status, forbidden substring or action, and acceptable response behavior.
Step 5  Run the probes through the application or a documented safe simulation.
Step 6  Apply deterministic checks for forbidden marker leakage, unauthorized action events, and terminal status.
Step 7  Manually rate whether refusals remain brief, respectful, and useful.
Step 8  Calculate pass rate by category and mark every safety failure as high severity.
Step 9  For each failure, identify whether the fix belongs in prompts, validation, tool permissions, approval flow, or logging.

activities.title: Build an Operational Evaluation Scorecard
activities.document_title: Session 6 Home Task 1 Build an Operational Evaluation Scorecard
activities.overview: Measure latency call usage failures and completion outcomes without a paid monitoring service.
activities.primary_output: A local operations evaluator and scorecard
instructions: Step 1  Define run_id, case_id, start time, end time, elapsed_ms, model_calls, tool_calls, retries, status, and sanitized error_type.
Step 2  Add instrumentation around the complete application call and every costly or failure-prone dependency.
Step 3  Run 20 cases that include success, validation rejection, model failure simulation, and tool failure simulation.
Step 4  Write one JSON object per run and confirm all IDs are unique.
Step 5  Calculate completion rate, rejection rate, error rate, retry rate, median latency, p95-style latency, average model calls, and maximum tool calls.
Step 6  Implement p95-style latency by sorting values and documenting the chosen nearest-rank rule.
Step 7  Break latency and error results down by terminal status or route.
Step 8  Set thresholds for four operational metrics and explain the user or resource reason for each threshold.
Step 9  Inspect the slowest three runs and every run that exceeded a call budget.
Step 10  Confirm submitted events contain no raw credentials, full prompts, or private conversation history.

activities.title: Create a Regression Suite and Release Gate
activities.document_title: Session 6 Home Task 2 Create a Regression Suite and Release Gate
activities.overview: Protect quality safety and operational behavior from silent changes.
activities.primary_output: An automated regression suite and release decision report
instructions: Step 1  Choose at least 18 regression cases and record why each case protects important behavior.
Step 2  Tag every case as deterministic, judge_required, safety_blocker, operational, or a combination.
Step 3  Define expected status, required checks, severity, and allowed variability for each case.
Step 4  Run deterministic checks first and stop judge calls for structurally invalid results.
Step 5  Run only the selected judge cases using a fixed rubric version.
Step 6  Calculate pass rate, safety pass rate, p95-style latency, and average model calls.
Step 7  Apply the starter release rules and add one rule for high-severity case IDs.
Step 8  Introduce one controlled prompt, route, retrieval, or threshold regression and rerun the identical suite.
Step 9  Record which tests fail, why they are useful, and whether the gate blocks release.
Step 10  Restore the intended behavior and rerun to a final decision.
Step 11  Save dataset, configuration, prompt, rubric, and code version labels in the report.

activities.title: Diagnose a Faulty RAG Pipeline
activities.document_title: Session 7 Class Activity 1 Diagnose a Faulty RAG Pipeline
activities.overview: Use component evidence to locate planted retrieval and generation defects.
activities.primary_output: A repaired RAG evaluator and diagnosis report
instructions: Step 1  Read the supplied document collection and label the relevant document for three direct questions.
Step 2  Run retrieve for each question and save ranked IDs before examining build_prompt.
Step 3  Calculate hit at 1 and first relevant rank for the three results.
Step 4  Write one assertion that should pass for each correct retrieval result and observe the failures.
Step 5  Inspect the ranking code and write a one-sentence defect hypothesis before changing it.
Step 6  Repair the ranking direction and rerun the unchanged retrieval tests.
Step 7  Inspect the generator prompt separately and identify wording that permits unsupported memory use.
Step 8  Rewrite the prompt to require context-only answers and an explicit insufficient-information response.
Step 9  Add two unanswerable questions and one context-conflict case.
Step 10  Use a fake deterministic generator or Gemini to verify that the prompt receives the intended context and rule.
Step 11  Run all tests and document baseline failure, first repair, second repair, and final result.

activities.title: Run a One Variable Improvement Experiment
activities.document_title: Session 7 Class Activity 2 Run a One Variable Improvement Experiment
activities.overview: Form a hypothesis change one variable and decide from paired evidence.
activities.primary_output: A baseline candidate comparison and decision log
instructions: Step 1  Group current failures and choose one pattern supported by at least two cases.
Step 2  Write the proposed cause and a prediction for affected and unaffected cases.
Step 3  Define a decision rule containing the target metric, minimum improvement, and maximum allowed regression severity.
Step 4  Freeze the baseline configuration and result file.
Step 5  Implement one primary variable change under a new configuration name.
Step 6  Run baseline and candidate on the identical eight or more cases.
Step 7  Create paired differences for retrieval rank, triad scores, deterministic checks, latency, and final status where available.
Step 8  Inspect every changed case and at least two unchanged control cases.
Step 9  Apply the decision rule without rewriting it after viewing results.
Step 10  Record keep, reject, or revise and name the next most informative experiment.

activities.title: Complete an End to End Evaluation Challenge
activities.document_title: Session 7 Home Task 1 Complete an End to End Evaluation Challenge
activities.overview: Evaluate an unfamiliar AI workflow locate its main failure and prove one improvement.
activities.primary_output: A complete diagnosis and improvement evidence pack
instructions: Step 1  Write the user goal, allowed scope, inputs, outputs, terminal states, and two critical safety requirements.
Step 2  Create at least 16 cases across normal, boundary, failure, and safety categories.
Step 3  Define deterministic checks and a short rubric before the first run.
Step 4  Run a black-box baseline and save every result, error, call count, and elapsed time.
Step 5  Calculate complete-case pass rate and at least three component or operational metrics relevant to the selected application.
Step 6  Read all high-severity failures and a sample of passes before inspecting implementation code.
Step 7  Map the largest failure pattern to the likely component and identify evidence that could disprove the diagnosis.
Step 8  Inspect the implementation and update the diagnosis without changing baseline cases.
Step 9  Implement one focused change and rerun the identical 16 cases.
Step 10  Compare paired outcomes, component metrics, safety results, and latency or call use.
Step 11  Run a regression check on all previously passing high-severity cases.
Step 12  Write a final decision including improvement, regression, uncertainty, and next action.

activities.title: Write an Evaluation Incident Report
activities.document_title: Session 7 Home Task 2 Write an Evaluation Incident Report
activities.overview: Reconstruct a silent quality regression identify the control gap and verify a durable fix.
activities.primary_output: An incident report and new regression protection
instructions: Step 1  Record the first known good version, change introduced, first bad run, detection time, fix, and verification run.
Step 2  Describe affected cases, metrics, routes, and user-visible behavior using saved evidence.
Step 3  State the actual observed impact and keep possible impact clearly labeled as a risk.
Step 4  Build a five-why chain or equivalent causal analysis that ends in a controllable system cause.
Step 5  Separate the root cause from contributing conditions such as weak coverage, missing gate, or unclear ownership.
Step 6  Explain why existing checks did not detect the regression before the bad run.
Step 7  Implement or document the corrective code or configuration change.
Step 8  Add at least one new regression case and one gate or process improvement.
Step 9  Show that the new case fails on the broken version and passes on the fixed version.
Step 10  Rerun the broader suite and report any side effects.
Step 11  Assign an owner and completion condition to every follow-up action.

activities.title: Review an Evaluation Suite Design
activities.document_title: Session 8 Class Activity 1 Review an Evaluation Suite Design
activities.overview: Check whether a capstone suite can support its intended quality claim before final runs begin.
activities.primary_output: A reviewed capstone evaluation dossier
instructions: Step 1  Write the application user, task, scope, non-goals, and one precise quality claim.
Step 2  List functional, quality, safety, and operational requirements with severity.
Step 3  Create 15 to 20 cases across ordinary, boundary, failure, and safety categories.
Step 4  Map every high-severity requirement to at least one case and one release rule.
Step 5  Choose at least one deterministic evaluator and one rubric-based evaluator.
Step 6  Explain how human labels are created independently from any judge being calibrated.
Step 7  Define baseline and candidate configurations with one primary difference.
Step 8  Set aggregate metrics, case-level blockers, call budget, and error handling.
Step 9  Exchange dossiers and conduct a ten-minute review using coverage, validity, reproducibility, safety, and feasibility checks.
Step 10  Record at least five findings with severity, response, and verification step.
Step 11  Resolve every high-severity finding before freezing the suite.

activities.title: Present an Evidence Based Evaluation Demo
activities.document_title: Session 8 Class Activity 2 Present an Evidence Based Evaluation Demo
activities.overview: Explain baseline diagnosis change and measured result in five minutes.
activities.primary_output: A timed demo script and peer scorecard
instructions: Step 1  Open with the application task and the exact quality question being tested.
Step 2  Show the case categories and explain why one average score is insufficient.
Step 3  Present the baseline with one headline metric and one representative failure.
Step 4  Explain the diagnosed component and the single primary change.
Step 5  Show paired baseline and candidate evidence for the representative failure.
Step 6  Report gains, regressions, safety blockers, and evaluator errors honestly.
Step 7  State the final keep, reject, or revise decision and one important limitation.
Step 8  Use a timeline of 30 seconds task, 45 seconds suite, 60 seconds baseline, 60 seconds diagnosis and change, 75 seconds comparison, and 30 seconds decision and limitation.
Step 9  Rehearse once, record actual time, and remove details that do not support the conclusion.
Step 10  Have a partner score claim clarity, evidence traceability, failure honesty, and time control.
Step 11  Revise the script once and record what changed.

activities.title: Package the Final Evaluation Capstone
activities.document_title: Session 8 Home Task 1 Package the Final Evaluation Capstone
activities.overview: Deliver a reproducible evaluation suite with a baseline one focused improvement and a defensible conclusion.
activities.primary_output: A complete Module 3 evaluation project ZIP
instructions: Step 1  Freeze the approved application scope, quality claim, requirements, and case set.
Step 2  Validate 15 to 20 case records and all expected values before model calls.
Step 3  Implement at least one deterministic evaluator and one structured rubric-based evaluator.
Step 4  Add the component evaluator relevant to the project such as retrieval, tool trace, route, approval, or abstention behavior.
Step 5  Include at least four safety or boundary cases and one case-level release blocker.
Step 6  Record model, prompt, rubric, dataset, application, and configuration version labels.
Step 7  Run the baseline and save complete sanitized case-level results.
Step 8  Diagnose the main failure pattern and write the candidate hypothesis before implementation.
Step 9  Apply one focused primary change and rerun the identical case set.
Step 10  Calculate paired case changes, aggregate metrics, safety results, latency, call use, and evaluator errors.
Step 11  Inspect every high-severity regression and all judge disagreements selected for review.
Step 12  Apply the predefined release rule and state keep, reject, or revise.
Step 13  Write a README with purpose, structure, setup, commands, expected artifacts, evaluation design, limitations, privacy, and troubleshooting.
Step 14  Run a clean-folder test using only the documented setup and commands.
Step 15  Scan the final folder for credentials, private data, caches, and absolute machine paths before creating the ZIP.

activities.title: Write the Evaluation Retrospective and Next Test Plan
activities.document_title: Session 8 Home Task 2 Write the Evaluation Retrospective and Next Test Plan
activities.overview: Assess the strength of the capstone evidence and prioritize the next evaluation work.
activities.primary_output: A final retrospective and prioritized evaluation backlog
instructions: Step 1  Restate the application scope, quality claim, and release decision exactly as used in the capstone.
Step 2  List each planned deliverable as completed, changed, deferred, or removed with a short reason.
Step 3  Summarize case counts, category coverage, evaluator success rate, key metrics, safety results, and operational results.
Step 4  Identify the three strongest pieces of evidence and explain which claim each supports.
Step 5  Identify the three weakest pieces of evidence and whether the weakness comes from data, labels, evaluator, sample size, or experiment design.
Step 6  Review false passes, false fails, evaluator errors, and high-severity regressions separately.
Step 7  List unresolved risks across quality, safety, privacy, operations, and evaluation validity.
Step 8  Create at least eight backlog items with value, risk reduced, effort, dependency, acceptance test, and evidence artifact.
Step 9  Prioritize three items using impact, uncertainty reduction, and effort.
Step 10  Write a two-week sequence for the three priorities without claiming production readiness.
Step 11  Define the condition that would change the current release decision.
